messages.subject: Problems with theme_set
parts:
Hi All

There is something about theme_set that I just don't get right. It
seems to have only one shot. E.g. in the script below, it works fine
on the first plot, but it seems to be ignored in the next. What am I
doing wrong?

m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x=rating))
m + geom_histogram()

my_theme <- theme_update(panel.background = theme_blank(), axis.text.x
= theme_text(colour = "black"), axis.text.y = theme_text(colour =
"black"), axis.title.x = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold", angle =
90), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.background = theme_blank(),
axis.line = theme_segment())

last_plot() + theme_set(my_theme)

#Looks fine, the theme was changed as I would expect.
#I then close the plot window and go on to make another plot.

hist_cut <-ggplot(diamonds, aes(x=price, fill=cut))
hist_cut + geom_bar()
last_plot()+ theme_set(my_theme)
# Now it seems like theme_set is ignored.
# Is this the normal behavior of theme_set() or have I messed
something up in the way I have created my_theme?

Best regards
Lars

messages.subject: Re: Problems with theme_set
parts:
Hi,

A lot of things occur here.

first,

my_theme <- theme_update(panel.background = theme_blank(), axis.text.x
= theme_text(colour = "black"), axis.text.y = theme_text(colour =
"black"), axis.title.x = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold", angle =
90), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.background = theme_blank(),
axis.line = theme_segment())

theme_set() and theme_update() modify the current theme and returns
*old* current theme.
so my_theme refers the old theme, and the current theme is the theme
that you gave.

then,

last_plot() + theme_set(my_theme)

the theme_set returns the old theme (i.e., one you gave), and set the
my_theme (i.e., default theme) as the current theme.
but this call have theme, the current theme is ignored and the theme
that theme_set() returned is used.

then, next call

last_plot() + theme_set(my_theme)

here, the current theme before the call is my_theme (i.e., default theme),
so theme_set returns the default theme.


finally, if you set the theme permanently in your session, then simply,

theme_update(panel.background = theme_blank(), axis.text.x
= theme_text(colour = "black"), axis.text.y = theme_text(colour =
"black"), axis.title.x = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold"),
axis.title.y = theme_text(colour = "black", face = "bold", angle =
90), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(),
panel.grid.major = theme_blank(), panel.background = theme_blank(),
axis.line = theme_segment())

qplot(1:2)
qplot(1:2, 3:4)

this is okey.


maybe my english is too poor to explain these things...
but hope this helps.

--
